newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Oppn urges govt not to sell art hoard.
newsitem.headline: Australian Oppn urges govt not to sell art hoard.

text.p: The Australian Labor opposition urged Prime Minister John Howard on Monday not to sell the government art collection.

Labor assumed that the sale of the collection, held by the government agency Artbank, was imminent because Arts Minister Richard Alston had publicly canvassed its value in a television interview earlier this month, a Labor official said.

"The financial case for selling Artbank is hard to establish, given its history of profitable operations and the fact that it hasn't drawn on the budget for any support for several years," Labor Arts Spokesman Bob McMullan said.
The Liberal-National government, which has sold several government assets since taking office last year, has never put a value on the collection.
